n6.vad-ligger-i-gpu-minnet.2: Once an inference server has started, GPU memory is split into four parts with completely different lifetimes:
n6.vad-ligger-i-gpu-minnet.7: the whole life of the server
n6.vad-ligger-i-gpu-minnet.10: one slot: for as long as a sequence lives
n6.vad-ligger-i-gpu-minnet.18: vLLM allocates the whole KV pool at startup. nvidia-smi therefore shows around 90% memory in use even when the server is completely idle. That is deliberate.
n6.vad-ligger-i-gpu-minnet.19: A larger token budget per step requires more room for activations, which leaves a smaller KV pool. Everything that is not weights is a trade-off between the two.
n6.vad-ligger-i-gpu-minnet.28: At startup vLLM logs the size of the pool:
n6.vad-ligger-i-gpu-minnet.31: The numbers for activations and overhead are approximate and vary.
n6.kv-cachen-pa-riktigt-en.1: The KV cache for real: a mini model
n6.kv-cachen-pa-riktigt-en.2: A real transformer runs here in your browser: 2 layers, 2 heads, d = 16, with attention, causal mask, RMSNorm and MLP. The weights are random, so the text is nonsense. The mechanics, however, are real.
n6.kv-cachen-pa-riktigt-en.3: Every step is computed in two ways:
n6.kv-cachen-pa-riktigt-en.4: Without a cache: the whole sequence is run again from the start.
n6.kv-cachen-pa-riktigt-en.5: With a cache: only the new token runs, K and V for the rest are read.
n6.kv-cachen-pa-riktigt-en.6: Compare the rightmost column: the difference in logits is zero or pure floating-point rounding. The KV cache is not an approximation.
n6.kv-cachen-pa-riktigt-en.7: The grid shows the actual K cache in layer 0, head 0. One row per position, and old rows never change.
n6.kapacitetsplanering.1: Capacity planning: is one GPU enough?
n6.kapacitetsplanering.2: Now you can answer the practical question: how many users can one GPU handle, and how fast is it for each of them?
n6.kapacitetsplanering.3: Do the weights fit? Parameters × bytes per parameter.
n6.kapacitetsplanering.4: How big is the KV pool? 90% of the memory minus weights minus about 5 GB.
n6.kapacitetsplanering.5: How many sequences fit? The pool divided by KV per sequence.
n6.kapacitetsplanering.6: How long is a decode step? Bytes to read (weights + all active KV) divided by the memory bandwidth.
n6.kapacitetsplanering.7: Step 3 gives the limit on concurrency. Step 4 gives the ITL for everyone in the batch.
n6.kapacitetsplanering.8: The model is idealized (H100-like bandwidth, no queues, all sequences the same length). Use it for orders of magnitude and to see which resource runs out first.
